name: omamail
title: Omamail — an Omarchy desktop mail client
summary: Mail as a native Omarchy window rather than a browser tab: a Quickshell plugin that reads, triages and answers mail over the Gmail API, over the HEY CLI, or over plain IMAP/SMTP for everything else. It runs inside the omarchy-shell process that is already there, follows the active theme, and puts an unread count in the bar. A desktop application, not a service — it exposes no HTTP surface of its own.

urls.install: install.sh — installs into the running omarchy-shell
urls.entryPoints: Service.qml (long-lived host) · BarWidget.qml (bar trigger) · App.qml (the window)

apps.role: the mail backends: Gmail API, HEY CLI, IMAP/SMTP, and the auth/credential managers behind them
the shared message resource every provider normalizes into
account state and the add-a-mailbox flow
local storage; the only layer allowed to persist
the interaction and layout primitives the feature views compose
the shell-facing widget and its settings bridge

auth: There is no server and no session: credentials belong to the person running the shell. Gmail uses OAuth through AuthManager, HEY delegates to the HEY CLI's own login, and IMAP/SMTP hold passwords in the local credential store (providers/Credentials.js). Nothing authenticates *to* Omamail.

integrations.how: HeyClient drives the official HEY CLI rather than scraping the web app
the fallback provider for everything else
the shell constructs Service.qml and hosts BarWidget.qml; the theme, fonts and density all come from the active Omarchy theme

gotchas: Five layers with dependencies pointing one way: shell entry points → window composition → domain modules → primitives → feature views. A view may ask the application to act, but must never reach for provider knowledge or mutate storage itself.

The visual system sits outside all five layers: colours, type, spacing, radii, icons and density come from the active Omarchy theme through App.qml and semantic component properties — never hard-coded.

GPUI and GPUI Component supply the architectural model (stable identity, explicit state ownership, controlled values, semantic events, behavior/presentation separation) translated into QML properties, signals and Qt lifecycle — not reproduced as Rust APIs.
The repository root holds only the QML entry points the shell loads. Service.qml owns what must outlive the window; App.qml owns navigation, focus context and non-popup surfaces.
A provider normalizes mail into the shared message resource and stops there — it never knows which row, popup or page is visible.
